stops.title: Options now carry into commands by default

mechanical.firstSentence: Options and most parsing settings set at the top level now carry into subcommands unless you mark them local.

judged.why: First sentence states the carry-into-subcommands change plainly, but the body gives framing/motivation rather than a specific thing to check.
First sentence ('Five things change for users') is a vague teaser, not a stated change, and the body is just an inventory with no flagged risk.

stops.title: Reset now keeps everything except local keys

mechanical.firstSentence: When yargs builds a subcommand, it now keeps every option, group and description except keys marked local (and their aliases).

judged.why: First sentence states the new keep-all-except-local reset behavior, and it flags that options.local is never cleared and persists across nesting.

stops.title: Global setter now also marks keys local

mechanical.firstSentence: Calling global with `false` now marks a key local, so it is dropped when a command runs.

judged.why: First sentence states that global(false) now marks a key local, and it directs the reviewer to verify global(true)/no-arg behavior is unchanged.

stops.title: Command validation now runs after the handler

mechanical.firstSentence: For subcommands, validation now runs after the handler has run, not before.

judged.why: First sentence states validation now runs after the handler, and explicit danger/mismatch flags point to specific risks to check.

stops.title: Checks, implies and conflicts carry into commands

mechanical.firstSentence: Custom checks now run inside subcommands unless you pass `false` as the second argument.

judged.why: First sentence states checks now run inside subcommands by default, and it flags the implies/conflicts auto-global override as worth checking.

stops.title: Strict mode carries into commands; false still enables it

mechanical.firstSentence: Calling strict now turns it on for all subcommands.

judged.why: First sentence states strict now carries into subcommands, and it flags the confusing strict(false) semantics and the never-reset flag.

stops.title: A false demandOption now makes the option required

mechanical.firstSentence: An option defined with `demandOption: false` is now treated as required.

judged.why: First sentence states demandOption:false now makes an option required, and an explicit danger flag calls this out as the opposite of its name.

mechanical.firstSentence: Calling demandCommand with no arguments now requires at least one command.

judged.why: First sentence states demandCommand with no args now requires at least one command, and it tells the reviewer to check nested re-declaration.

stops.title: Tests for the new defaults and opt-outs

mechanical.firstSentence: The new tests check that config, implies, conflicts, checks, demandOption, strict, array, choices, alias, coerce, defaults, describe, help, version and groups carry into commands, and that each has a `global: false` opt-out.

judged.why: First sentence describes what the new tests check rather than a behavior change, but it does name specific untested gaps worth checking.
